item.content:encoded:
Upvoted.

The thing that occurred to me is near the end, where it did the matrix multiplication, more activity was observed on the left side of the SCP than the right. I'll admit this is wild speculation on my part and is a bit of a leap. People who are 'left-brained' are considered logical thinkers while people who are 'right-brained' are better at creativity. The whole left / right thing near the end of the SCP reminded me of that, and I jumped to the idea of "What if this thing is a physical manifestation of something's brain? What sort of creature would be capable of the feats so far demonstrated???"

That could easily get Keter level if it turned out to be the case.

item.content:encoded:
"Furthermore, the subsequent arrangement of SCP-468-2 facilitated fraction multiplication, the only recorded instance of a decrease in mathematical complexity between rearrangement periods."

This freaks me right out. Linear mathematical progression is less unnerving than non-linear progression, which removes the capacity to plot the item's progression in the future and brings up some really uneasy questions.

Typically speaking, you move back to basics from more complex equations to try and build a different approach to the problem at hand.

But what is it solving for, then?

I liked this one, upvoted.

That being said, two lines jumped out at me, so I am here to go all anal retentive up this bitch.

"All sufficiently large animals, such as horses, dogs, cats, and human beings, within SCP-468-2 are subject to its effects." -You have some weird commas going on here, needs cleaning up.

"SCP-468-1’s beads will often perform basic arithmetic operations, though this is occasionally not the case." -The word "occasionally" feels really off here. Probably grammatically correct, but just feels awkward. Maybe "this is not always the case" or something.
